system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Venice, . Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Venice itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Venice space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (San Marco, Dorsoduro, Cannaregio, Castello, Giudecca) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Venice spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Venice, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Victoria Miro Venice
galleries.address_hint: Il Capricorno, San Marco 1994, Calle Drio la Chiesa
galleries.note: Venice outpost of the London mega-gallery, in the historic Il Capricorno space; shows Grayson Perry, Chris Ofili, Yayoi Kusama and others, and is the city's strongest international commercial programme.

galleries.name: Galleria Michela Rizzo
galleries.note: The most ambitious Venetian-owned contemporary gallery, with a large Giudecca warehouse space, a research-driven programme and consistent Italian art-fair presence.

galleries.name: Galleria Alberta Pane
galleries.note: Paris–Venice gallery showing an international roster of conceptual and performance-based artists; regular at Artissima, Art Brussels and Paris fairs.

galleries.name: Marignana Arte
galleries.note: Rigorous programme bridging Italian post-war abstraction and younger conceptual practices; a fixture of Venice's Biennale-season calendar and of Italian fairs.

galleries.name: Ocean Space (TBA21–Academy)
galleries.address_hint: Chiesa di San Lorenzo, Campo San Lorenzo, Castello 5069
galleries.note: TBA21–Academy's commissioning platform in a deconsecrated church, pairing major artist commissions with ocean research; internationally the most-discussed non-Biennale venue in the city.

galleries.name: Fondazione Bevilacqua La Masa
galleries.address_hint: Piazza San Marco 71/c; Palazzetto Tito, Dorsoduro 2826
galleries.note: Founded 1898, the city's historic incubator for emerging artists, with studios, an annual open call and two public exhibition spaces.

galleries.name: Alma Zevi
galleries.note: Curatorially sharp gallery mixing modern estates with young international artists; a key stop for the visiting art world during Biennale openings.

galleries.name: A plus A Gallery
galleries.note: Slovenian exhibition centre turned experimental gallery and school platform; long history of Central/Eastern European and emerging Italian shows.

galleries.name: Berggruen Arts & Culture – Palazzo Diedo
galleries.note: Restored palazzo opened 2024 with permanent site-specific commissions (Sterling Ruby, Urs Fischer, Lee Ufan) and a residency; instantly a major Venice venue.

galleries.name: Fondazione Emilio e Annabianca Vedova
galleries.note: Artist's foundation in a Renzo Piano-adapted salt warehouse; exhibitions of Vedova alongside leading international contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Caterina Tognon Arte Contemporanea
galleries.note: The reference gallery for contemporary art in glass, working with international artists and museums since 1992.

galleries.name: Berengo Studio / Fondazione Berengo
galleries.address_hint: Fondamenta Vetrai 109/A and Campiello della Pescheria, Murano
galleries.note: Furnace, gallery and foundation behind 'Glasstress', which has brought hundreds of major contemporary artists to work in Murano glass.

galleries.name: S.a.L.E. Docks
galleries.note: Independent, occupation-born collective space for politically engaged art, activism and experimental programming; a critical counter-voice to the Biennale economy.

galleries.name: Le Stanze del Vetro
galleries.address_hint: Fondazione Giorgio Cini, Isola di San Giorgio Maggiore
galleries.note: Free exhibition space devoted to 20th-century and contemporary glass, with scholarly, museum-quality shows and a permanent study centre.

galleries.name: Espace Louis Vuitton Venezia
galleries.note: Free corporate exhibition space presenting works from the Fondation Louis Vuitton collection and solo projects by internationally established artists.

galleries.name: Spazio Punch
galleries.note: Independent space in a former brewery known for design-adjacent, experimental and youth-driven exhibitions and collaborations.

galleries.name: Ikona Gallery
galleries.note: Long-running photography gallery in the Ghetto, run by Živa Kraus since 1979, with a strong documentary and Central European emphasis.

galleries.name: Jarach Gallery
galleries.note: Photography- and lens-based gallery next to La Fenice, showing international names and Venice-specific commissions.

galleries.name: Beatrice Burati Anderson Art Space & Gallery
galleries.note: Curator-run gallery with a lively programme of emerging Italian and international artists and Biennale-season collateral projects.

galleries.name: Galleria d'Arte Contini
galleries.address_hint: Calle dello Spezier 2765 and San Marco 2288, Campo Santo Stefano
galleries.note: The city's largest commercial operation, with modern masters and blue-chip contemporary names plus high-visibility public installations.

galleries.name: Bugno Art Gallery
galleries.note: Established Venetian dealer of postwar and contemporary Italian art, active since the 1990s with a busy exhibition calendar.

galleries.name: Galleria Ravagnan
galleries.note: Family gallery in Piazza San Marco since 1967, mixing historic Venetian modernism with contemporary sculpture and glass.

galleries.name: Galleria Il Traghetto
galleries.note: One of Venice's oldest continuously running contemporary galleries (since 1968), with deep roots in the Italian postwar scene.

galleries.name: Emily Harvey Foundation
galleries.note: Fluxus-linked residency and exhibition space continuing the legacy of the New York dealer; small but internationally networked.

galleries.name: Microclima
galleries.address_hint: Serra dei Giardini, Via Giuseppe Garibaldi 1254
galleries.note: Curatorial platform in the Giardini's historic greenhouse, producing site-specific projects, talks and artist commissions year-round.

galleries.name: Zuecca Projects
galleries.note: Producer of architecture and art exhibitions and Biennale collateral events, with a project space on the Giudecca waterfront.

galleries.name: CREA Cantieri del Contemporaneo
galleries.address_hint: Giudecca 211, ex convento dei SS. Cosma e Damiano
galleries.note: Studios, residencies and exhibition halls in a former convent; a hub for the Giudecca Art District and local artist community.

galleries.name: Nuova Icona
galleries.address_hint: Giudecca; also Oratorio di San Ludovico, Dorsoduro
galleries.note: Artist-run association active since 1993, producing exhibitions and Biennale collateral projects in unusual sacred spaces.

galleries.name: Spazio Berlendis
galleries.note: Large independent hall near Fondamente Nove hosting national pavilions, collateral events and ambitious guest-curated shows.

galleries.name: Galerie Dorothea van der Koelen
galleries.note: Mainz-based gallery's Venice space, showing concrete, minimal and light-based artists such as Mack, Morellet and Venet.

galleries.name: European Cultural Centre (Palazzo Mora / Palazzo Bembo)
galleries.note: Runs the sprawling 'Personal Structures' exhibitions across two palazzi; hugely visible during Biennale years, if divisive critically.

galleries.name: Fondazione dell'Albero d'Oro – Palazzo Vendramin Grimani
galleries.address_hint: Palazzo Vendramin Grimani, Campo San Polo 2033
galleries.note: Restored palazzo staging carefully curated dialogues between contemporary artists and Venetian history.

galleries.name: Ca' Foscari Esposizioni / Spazio Ca' Foscari Zattere
galleries.note: University exhibition spaces presenting research-based contemporary shows and Biennale collateral events open to the public.

galleries.name: Galleria del Cavallino
galleries.note: Historic gallery and publishing house founded by Carlo Cardazzo in 1942 — central to Spatialism and Italian video art — still active with its archive and editions.

galleries.name: Venice Projects
galleries.note: Marino Barovier's gallery for contemporary and historic studio glass and design, respected for its scholarship and museum collaborations.

galleries.name: Melori & Rosenberg Gallery
galleries.note: Ghetto gallery combining contemporary painting and Judaica-related programming; long-standing presence in Cannaregio.

galleries.name: Giudecca 795 Art Gallery
galleries.note: Small waterfront gallery central to the Giudecca Art District, showing emerging and mid-career Italian artists.

galleries.name: Officina delle Zattere
galleries.note: Flexible exhibition venue on the Zattere used for independent contemporary shows and Biennale-period projects.

galleries.name: Spazio Thetis
galleries.note: Industrial site inside the Arsenale hosting large-scale sculpture, national participations and collateral exhibitions since the 1990s.

galleries.name: Galleria d'Arte L'Occhio
galleries.address_hint: Dorsoduro 181, near Santa Maria della Salute
galleries.note: Long-established gallery showing contemporary painting, sculpture and glass by Italian and international artists.

galleries.name: Holly Snapp Gallery
galleries.note: Anglo-Venetian gallery of long standing, best known for the work of Geoffrey Humphries and figurative painters working in Venice.

galleries.name: SMAC – San Marco Art Centre
galleries.note: Exhibition centre opened 2025 on the piano nobile above Piazza San Marco, programming international art and architecture shows.

galleries.name: Bel-Air Fine Art Venise
galleries.note: Venice branch of the Geneva-based chain; commercially prominent pop and urban-art programme in the San Marco tourist core.

galleries.name: Combo Venezia
galleries.address_hint: Campo dei Gesuiti 4878, ex Convento dei Crociferi
galleries.note: Cultural hub in a former convent whose gallery hosts free contemporary exhibitions, screenings and residencies aimed at younger audiences.

galleries.name: Fallani Venezia
galleries.note: Historic serigraphy workshop that doubles as an exhibition space, printing editions with international contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Marina Bastianello Gallery
galleries.note: Mainland gallery with a young, digitally engaged programme and a solid Italian fair presence; part of the wider Venetian scene.

galleries.name: Galleria Massimo De Luca
galleries.note: Research-minded mainland gallery supporting emerging Veneto artists with a curatorial, non-commercial-first approach.

galleries.name: Casa Sanlorenzo
galleries.note: Corporate-backed art hub opened 2025 in a restored palazzo, offering exhibitions, a residency and public programming.

galleries.name: Galleria Santo Stefano
galleries.note: Veteran central gallery handling modern and contemporary Italian painting and sculpture with regular seasonal shows.

galleries.name: Galleria San Vidal
galleries.note: Established San Marco dealer combining 20th-century Italian art with contemporary figurative painting and glass.
